Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The new 2025 national ID card has digital authentication capabilities: an RFID chip storing biometric data and a digital certificate, a QR code with ICAO Datastructure for Barcodes digital signature, and an MRZ. The card enables 'strong electronic authentication by means of a digital certificate issued by the card-issuing authority' for e-government services. Hand-held scanners can verify digitally.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The new 2025 system includes online pre-enrollment via the idcam.cm government portal. The digital ID card is designed to allow 'secure access to electronic services such as e-government via Internet portals.' The system provides e-government access through digital certificates embedded in the card.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No evidence of a citizen-facing portal for individuals to view or manage their own stored identity data. While the new system has online pre-enrollment (idcam.cm), this is for application only. World Bank ID4D noted no self-service data access mechanisms. Law 2024/017 grants data subject rights including access rights, but implementation infrastructure is not yet in place.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The national ID enables KYC for financial services. Law No. 2010/012 mandates financial institutions to verify customer identities using official ID. The NID is required for bank account opening, mobile money registration, and other financial services KYC. Third-party KYC providers (Smile ID, VOVE ID) actively verify Cameroonian national IDs.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: General judicial oversight exists through the court system. Law 90-42 provides for criminal penalties for not carrying an ID card. Courts handle nationality fraud cases and late birth registration disputes. However, there is no specific judicial mechanism dedicated to ID system oversight or biometric data oversight.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: World Bank ID4D diagnostic (2024) confirmed no integration between civil registration and ID systems: only manual visual checks of birth certificates are performed. No digital data sharing exists. The 2024 civil registration law (No. 2024/016) introduces a UPIN at birth, but linkage with the adult ID system is still planned and not yet operational.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Partially available. Law 2024/017 (Data Protection Act) provides a framework for data sharing with consent requirements. Civil registration law 2024/016 grants public administrations access to the national civil status database. However, operational interoperability between the ID system and sectoral systems remains absent in practice; rules are still being developed.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No comprehensive standalone digital ID regulation exists. Decree 2025/059 governs ID card issuance but does not constitute a full digital ID law. World Bank (2024) noted lack of a robust legal framework to regulate digital identity specifically. The new system article (We Are Tech, Feb 2025) explicitly states Cameroon must still establish a strong legal framework for digital identity.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on Personal Data Protection was enacted, making Cameroon the 38th African country with comprehensive data protection legislation. It covers data subject rights (access, erasure, portability), data processing obligations, cross-border transfer restrictions, and creates a supervisory authority. Previously, Law No. 2010/013 provided partial data protection provisions.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Law No. 2024/017 establishes the Personal Data Protection Authority (Autorité de protection des données à caractère personnel) responsible for regulating data protection and issuing rules. Previously, CNIL (Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés) existed under Law 2010/013 and is referenced by financial service providers as the oversight body. The new authority was legally created in December 2024.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The National Identity Card serves as legal proof of identity and nationality for all official transactions. It is mandatory for voting, opening bank accounts, SIM registration, accessing government services, and legal transactions. Decree 2025/059 defines five legally recognized identity documents.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Legal framework exists: Law No. 90-042 of 19 December 1990 (mandatory national ID for citizens 18+, with criminal penalties); Decree No. 2016/375 of 04 August 2016 (ID card characteristics); Decree No. 2025/059 of 28 February 2025 (new ID card regulations recognizing 5 identity documents). New civil registration law No. 2024/016 of 23 December 2024 also enacted.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: In May 2024, DGSN signed a 15-year build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract with German firm Augentic for the new ID system. Previous contracts were with French companies Gemalto (acquired by Thales). Core system design, production, and operation is dominated by foreign vendors, though DGSN retains institutional oversight.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance has partial oversight through: regulation of stamp duty fees for ID applications (10,000 FCFA per 2025 Tax Code), coordination of financial inclusion policies, and AML compliance strategies via ANIF. However, the national ID system budget and operations are primarily managed by the DGSN under the Presidency, not the Ministry of Finance directly.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: World Bank ID4D (2024) found insufficient domestic financing: insufficient funding, donor-funded pilots are fragmented, the PRE2C committee became inactive due to funding lapses, and recommendations called for pooled donor financing. The new 2025 system relies on a 15-year BOT contract with private foreign capital (Augentic). Financing is primarily external/private sector.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The new 2025 national ID card captures 10 fingerprints and a facial photograph at enrollment. The RFID chip stores biographic data plus two encrypted fingerprints and a digital photo. AFIS (Automatic Fingerprint Identification System) is used for 1:n biometric deduplication.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Cameroon has maintained a fully digital centralized identity database since 1994. The DGSN operates a physical data center with backup. Data is encrypted and transmitted via FTP/VPN/USB. AFIS-based biometric deduplication is in place. The 2025 system further modernizes this infrastructure.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Cameroon launched its new biometric digital ID system in February 2025, with nationwide rollout. A digital ID system has existed since 1994 (computerized) and 2016 (biometric smart card). The 2025 system with Augentic is progressively being deployed across all regional capitals.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: No digital interoperability between the national ID system and other government systems (health, social protection, civil registration). World Bank ID4D diagnostic (2024) confirmed: no data sharing between CR and ID systems; only manual visual checks of breeder documents. An inter-ministerial committee is developing an Infocentre for harmonization but not yet operational.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The national ID card is not free. The 2025 stamp duty is 10,000 FCFA (~USD 18) per the 2025 Tax Code, up from 2,800 FCFA (~USD 4.50) previously. Total actual costs including nationality certificate, birth certificate certification, and internet access are estimated at ~20,000 FCFA (~USD 36). Cameroon lawmakers have criticized the cost as prohibitively high.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Cameroon's new 2025 ID card is ICAO Doc 9303 compliant (TD1 format, MRZ, biometric chip), enabling recognition at international checkpoints. Some regional recognition exists within CEMAC (free movement zone covering Cameroon, Chad, Congo, DRC). However, formal digital interoperability agreements for cross-border electronic authentication have not been established.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Enrollment in the National Identity Card system is restricted to citizens aged 18 and over. Decree 2025/059 and Keesing Platform confirm: 'All Cameroon citizens aged 18 and over are required to register for and carry the National Identity Card.' No provision for persons under 18 to enroll in the national ID.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is mandatory for all Cameroonian citizens aged 18 and above. Law No. 90-42 of 19 December 1990 provides criminal penalties (3 months to 1 year imprisonment or fine of 50,000-100,000 FCFA) for citizens not possessing a national identity card. No direct sanctions for failing to apply, but required for all public services.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Some non-nationals are eligible for identity documents. Decree 2025/059 recognizes: Residence Permit, Permanent Resident Card (for long-term legal residents), and Refugee Card (for registered refugees via UNHCR and MINREX). World Bank ID4D noted a refugee pilot program issuing ~5,000 cards to refugees (of ~230,000 eligible). Not all non-nationals are eligible.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: World Bank ID4D diagnostic (2024): approximately 82.8% of eligible adults (18+) have a national ID, with an estimated 2.5 million adults lacking ID. However, Aug 2025 sources note less than one quarter of all Cameroonians hold valid identity documents (which includes children). Using adult eligibility coverage (~82.8%), this falls in the 70-89% range.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Security measures are in place: encrypted data storage, VPN/FTP transmission, physical data center security, AFIS biometric deduplication, and ICAO-compliant digital signature verification on the new card. The cybersecurity law (No. 2010/012) applies. The January 2025 duplicate identity cleanup operation included an interministerial security review. No publicly documented independent external security audit specifically for the ID system.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration requires a national ID card (or passport). World Bank ID4D confirmed NID is mandatory for SIM registration with a maximum of 12 SIMs per ID. This blocks mobile money access for many. Pikasim (eSIM provider) confirms: 'Cameroon requires SIM registration with national ID or passport.'

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID is required to access social protection programs. World Bank ID4D confirmed ID is needed for cash transfers (Projet Filets Sociaux/PFS), pensions (CNPS), and the planned Unified Social Registry. UNAIDS/WFP cash transfer program noted that ID card was required for beneficiaries to collect funds, causing exclusion for those without IDs.
